subject: Offset time formats
notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A plus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC' -> OK, anchored on the rule marker '1)' under (Offset subformats). The rule has two obligation halves and I read BOTH. (1) PRODUCE-THE-CHARACTER. CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 361-363 is the ONE renderer of a §15.3 offset subformat's sign: 'long offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes); int oh = (int)(offMag/60), om = (int)(offMag%60); char osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-';', emitted at 'case Fld.OffSign: sb.Append(osign)'. argument-4 of FORMATTED-DATETIME / argument-3 of FORMATTED-TIME is 'the offset from UTC expressed in minutes' (§15.40.3 r5 --check OK), so a NON-NEGATIVE argument means local is at or ahead of UTC and the sign written is '+', which is exactly what rule 1 makes '+' mean. Verified by golden: conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'T-OFF=01:00:00+01:00' (offset 60) and 'OFF-MAX=010000+2359' (offset 1439), conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/formatted_datetime 'T3=123456+0200' (offset 120). (2) HONOUR-THE-MEANING. The direction rule 1 fixes is what §15.40.4 r2 / §15.41.4 r2 ('the time portion ... reflects the adjustment of the value in argument-3 by the offset in argument-4' -- --check OK) leaves unstated; EmitFormatted lines 326-330 implement it as 'if (hasTime && isUtc && hasOffset) { secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m; ... }' -- a POSITIVE offset SUBTRACTS, i.e. adjusts the common time DOWNWARD to represent UTC. Verified by golden: conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/formatted_datetime 'T2=10:34:56Z' from local 45296 s (12:34:56) with offset +120, and conformance:cases/_unassigned/r25_utc_roll_date_range case 4 'FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ" 2 0 1439)' -> '16010101T000100Z' (1601-01-02 00:00:00 minus 23h59m). (3) CONSUME-THE-CHARACTER. CobolDate.cs#Analyze lines 510-516 accept '+' in the sign position; the sign is deliberately NOT applied downstream, which is correct and not a gap: §15.79.4 makes SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME's value ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) over the hours/minutes/seconds subfields only (--check OK) and §15.48.4 r1's NOTE says the time portion of a combined format 'is validated against the format ... but if valid does not impact the returned value'. Pinned by conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form, which runs the standard's own D.31.5.8/D.31.5.9 worked examples: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500") = 0143951 (identical to the date-only form) and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss.ss+hhmm", "05142781+0500") = 18867.81 (= 5*3600+14*60+27.81, the offset NOT applied). No second renderer exists: grepping the whole of src/ for '+' : '-' returns only EmitFormatted line 363 and Format21 line 35, and Format21 serves §15.21.3/§15.99's separate 21-character layout, not a §15.3 offset subformat. FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE reaches the same one renderer (CobolDate.cs#FormattedCurrentDate passes now.Offset.TotalMinutes), so the system-clock producer inherits the same sign convention. Editions 2014,2023: the offset subformat is reachable ONLY through the FORMATTED-*/INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE/SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME/TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME family, which the inventory's already-adjudicated §15.38-§15.48/§15.79/§15.92 rows uniformly window at 2014,2023; Annex E documents only the 2014->2023 delta and lists no change here, so there is no 2023 delta either. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS, but the EVIDENCE CHAIN is corrected and the record changed. (1) CITATION re-derived independently: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A plus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC' -> OK, anchored on the rule marker '1)' under (Offset subformats); I also re-derived §15.40.3 r5, §15.40.4 r2/r3, §15.41.3 r4/r6, §15.41.4 r2/r3, §15.48.4 r1 and §15.79.4 r1 by reading §15.40-§15.41/§15.48/§15.79 whole rather than trusting the adjudicator's quotes. (2) TEST-REF CORRECTED: conformance:cases/_unassigned/r25_utc_roll_date_range is REMOVED. Every one of its five cases uses the format 'YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ', which by §15.3.3.5 is a common time format followed by a single 'Z' and therefore carries NO offset subformat and emits NO sign character at all -- it cannot close a rule about the character in 'the data associated with an offset subformat'. It is evidence for §15.40.4 r2 (a separately inventoried row, RV-15.40.4-2), not for this one. (3) WHAT ACTUALLY CLOSES THE MEANING HALF, which the adjudicator did not identify: conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/formatted_datetime renders the SAME instant twice from the SAME operands -- T2=10:34:56Z and T3=123456+0200, both from WS-SEC=45296 with offset 120 -- so the golden itself asserts 12:34:56+02:00 == 10:34:56Z, which IS the §15.3.3.6.1 NOTE-1 equivalence and is a real closure of 'adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC'. (4) SECOND-BODY SWEEP RUN INDEPENDENTLY, not inherited: grep over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.* for OffSign|OffHour|OffMinute|offZero returns CobolDate.cs and nothing else (Tokenize 275/260/262, EmitFormatted 382-384, Analyze 510-531); CobolDate.Format21 is the only other offset-sign writer and serves §15.21.3/§15.99.3's separate 21-character layout; RuntimeApi.DateFn emits 'CobolDate.<method>(...)' and the checked-in generated source tests/conformance/2023/formatted_time_seconds_channel.g.cs confirms the call lands on CobolDate.FormattedTime, not on the legacy src/Legacy.Runtime IntrinsicFunctions.FormattedTime(string,decimal) (which has no offset parameter at all and is the opt-in oracle, out of scope). (5) TWO-ARM RISK MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderDec returns null for this family (not in its switch, alwaysDec false, and AnyDecOrRealRaw is false because the arguments are strings), so the native arm at IntrinsicRenderer.cs cases 324/326/334 and the string arm at 921-926 are the only lanes and both call the one runtime body. (6) Both cited goldens are ENABLED (not pending) in tests/conformance/2014/manifest.json and .../2023/manifest.json -- checked, because a pending fixture would make the test-ref inert.
